name: H3-nozzle
prompt:
Image 1 is a motor-axis layout guide only. Replace dots and lines with a complete industrial product and omit all visible guide marks.
Design a flat hexacopter for civil agricultural crop care. Strict orthographic top view, nose toward the top edge of the image, arms fully unfolded.
Six motors in a Radial hex layout: six motor centres at the corners of a regular hexagon. Mean opposite-motor (diagonal) span 1400 mm; motor-centre width-to-length span ratio W/L 1.15; adjacent arm angles clockwise from the first motor: 60°, 60°, 60°, 60°, 60°, 60°.
Match the motor centres and frame links in the attached layout image: dots mark motor centres, lines mark frame links. Do not reproduce the dots or lines in the result.
Each motor carries one stationary 2-blade propeller, 20-inch (508 mm) diameter. The two blades point in exactly opposite directions from the hub.
No propeller guards.
Each arm is 15 mm wide and 4 mm thick; seen from above it reads as a 15 mm wide beam.
Each arm is attached to the shell by a visible folding hinge with a pivot pin.
Fuselage design envelope 100 × 80 × 30 mm (length × width × height); this is a size limit, not a shape.
A square spray tank sits half-embedded in the central frame: the frame wraps the lower half of the tank, while the tank top and its round filler cap stay exposed.
No camera or gimbal is fitted.
There is no spray boom. Instead, one small round spray nozzle is mounted directly below each of the six motors, its dark nozzle tip just visible beside the motor from above.
Low landing skids with 40 mm ground clearance, tucked beneath the aircraft.
Show the complete product on a plain light background as a photorealistic industrial design rendering. Omit guide marks, dimensions and lettering.
negative_prompt: flat schematic, line drawing, collage, text, labels, logo, cropped rotor, disconnected arm, extra rotor, perspective camera, V-shaped propeller, blades at an acute angle, single-blade propeller, missing blade, unequal blades
